subject: Cross-border forensics & evidence transfer — scope & jurisdictional queries
messages:
From: danielle.perez@atlasbank.com
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai; marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: legal_ops@atlasbank.com
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: forensic scope + cross-border evidence handback

Jordan / Marissa —

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. We need to firm up a couple of points so our incident response obligations to the EU regulator are covered. High-level asks from Atlas legal/security: 

- Precise timeline for how long Redwood persists unredacted user inputs in any persistent store or exportable backups (not transient KV caches).
- Whether Redwood can produce a time-bounded forensic snapshot (UTC timestamps, inclusive) for a 72-hour window around an incident and whether that snapshot can be exported to an EU-only SFTP for our forensics team.
- Confirmation of which subprocessors (and their region) would have access to any exported evidence. We need a subprocessor map with region flags.
- Contractual assurances re: transfer mechanisms — if cross-border transfer is required, we need the legal mechanism (SCCs, adequacy, or specific customer-facing DPA clause).

I'm attaching a very short template of the forensics request the regulator expects. Can Redwood review and confirm feasibility + any lead time required?

Danielle
Security Incident Response 
Atlas Bank

Attachment: forensic_request_template.pdf (1 page)

From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: danielle.perez@atlasbank.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai; ben_carter@redwood.ai; laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: forensic scope + cross-border evidence handback

Danielle —

Appreciate the clear asks. Looping in Marissa (Legal) and Ben (Account Lead / Ops) so we can cover legal, operational, and sales requirements. Quick responses below; we'll follow with a short runbook and timeline by EOD Monday.

1) Persistence of unredacted inputs:
- Short answer: Redwood does not persist unredacted user inputs in long-term object stores by default for hosted accounts. However, there are two places to call out:
  * S3 exports for customers who have enabled audit exports (opt-in) — those are customer-owned buckets and retention is governed by the customer's lifecycle policy.
  * Forensic/incident snapshots produced by internal ops at customer request — these are produced on-demand and stored in a gated evidence store.

2) Forensic snapshot window / export:
- We can produce a 72-hour UTC-bounded forensic bundle. The bundle includes request/response logs, model selection metadata, and (if available) the ephemeral KV cache at the requested timestamps.
- Export options: EU-only SFTP or a pre-approved AWS EU S3 bucket (customer-owned). We do NOT push evidence to third-party cloud buckets without prior approval.

3) Subprocessor access:
- We'll provide an export of current subprocessors and region tags. Most infra subprocessors operate in multi-region clusters; only a small set of maintenance vendors (listed in subprocessor_map_v2.csv) have access to backups for recovery.

4) Cross-border legal mechanism:
- For hosted customers, we rely on SCCs + DPA clauses we already offer. For Dedicated/Private customers we can adopt contractual language or rely on adequacy when applicable. Marissa will confirm exact clause references.

Next steps: Ben will confirm technical lead time for a forensic bundle; Marissa will propose the contract language we should sign off for this specific exchange (DocuSign link preferred to record acceptance).

Thanks — Jordan
Head of Account Success, Redwood Inference

--

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai; ben_carter@redwood.ai; laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: forensic scope + cross-border evidence handback

Danielle —

Thanks for the template — helpful. A few legal clarifications before we proceed with an evidence export: 

- Scope definition: Redwood is comfortable producing logs, model metadata, and snapshots of ephemeral caches, but we treat customer-owned persisted exports (S3) as under the customer's control. Any request that requires Redwood to retrieve data from a customer-owned backup will require the customer to provide access/credentials or to transfer the backup to a Redwood-controlled evidence container under an agreed transfer method.

- Redaction / minimization: For regulatory submissions we can run a minimization pass to remove unrelated tenant identifiers, but we need the explicit scope (user IDs, session IDs, or query hashes) to avoid over-redaction.

- Subprocessor access: We'll provide the current CSV of subprocessors and region flags. Note: maintenance subprocessors in APAC will not be granted access to EU-only evidence exports. Access is controlled via role-based policies; we record all access events in our audit log.

- Legal mechanism for transfers: We propose signing a short addendum to our DPA referencing SCCs for any temporary transfers outside the EU for the sole purpose of forensic analysis. If Atlas prefers evidence to remain in the EU at all times, we will export to an EU-only bucket or SFTP under the customer's control.

Please confirm: (A) whether Atlas will provide an EU S3 bucket / SFTP endpoint or (B) would like Redwood to provision an EU-only evidence container (requires signed addendum).

If you confirm option A we can produce the 72-hour bundle within 48 hours of receiving the endpoint and the exact UTC window. If option B, allow 5 business days for provisioning and legal sign-off.

Marissa 
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: subprocessor_map_v2.csv (generated snapshot)

From: danielle.perez@atlasbank.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai; jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai; laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: forensic scope + cross-border evidence handback

Marissa / Jordan —

Thanks — Atlas will provide an EU S3 bucket (we'll share credentials via secure transfer) and we prefer the 72-hour bundle to be placed there. We'll also sign the short addendum; please send the DocuSign link.

Scope for minimization: please keep the snapshot to sessions with these session IDs: sess-1a9f, sess-2b7c, sess-33ef and any associated request/response pairs. Do not include any other tenants.

Timelines: we need the bundle deposited within 72 hours of our credentials delivery if possible. Please confirm when you receive the S3 details and the DocuSign envelope.

Danielle
Security Incident Response 
Atlas Bank

--
